wolf.line: In a yellow El Camino, listening to Howlin' Wolf
stanza: We used to drive through Lafayette to Baton Rogue
In a yellow El Camino, listening to Howlin' Wolf
He liked to stop in Lake Charles because that's the place he loved
Did you run about as far as you could go?
Down the Louisiana highway, across Lake Pontchartrain?
Now your soul is in Lake Charles, no matter what they say

wolf.line: And I try to calm the wolf
stanza: My dog barks wildly
To protect my infancy
From my ex-believer
And I try to calm the wolf
To remind her I am both
Still she tears at my sweater

wolf.line: You know more folks is most afraid of the wolf
wolf.linePrev: Hidden amongst all those troubled souls
wolf.lineNext: But if you really stop and think

wolf.line: I'm not afraid of the gray wolf
stanza: I'm not afraid of the gray wolf
Who stalks through our forest at dawn
As long as I have her beside me
I have the strength to carry on
Though it's fearful
Though it's deep, though it's dark
And though you may lose the path
Though you may encounter wolves
You can't just act
You have to listen
You can't just act
You have to think
